subject.title: Android node notification forwarding causes cross-session replies (WhatsApp duplicate sends to wrong group)

question: Should OpenClaw enforce the fix primarily at outbound session/channel binding, Android native-package notification suppression, Gateway notification package filtering, or a layered combination?
rationale: The remaining path crosses Android notification policy, Gateway node-session events, and possible heartbeat-driven outbound delivery; choosing the wrong owner could leave a cross-channel security gap or add brittle package/config policy.

options.title: Harden outbound binding first
options.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel sends from node notification or heartbeat sessions unless an explicit verified route binding exists, then use Android or Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

options.title: Suppress native packages in Android
options.body: Default-block known native-channel Android package IDs, reducing duplicate inputs but requiring maintained package ownership policy.

options.title: Add Gateway package filtering
options.body: Add server-side package filtering for notification events, which helps operators but adds config/default-surface and does not by itself settle outbound authority.

recommendation.title: Harden outbound binding first
recommendation.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel sends from node notification or heartbeat sessions unless an explicit verified route binding exists, then use Android or Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: The core decision centers on the Gateway/node notification event path and its interaction with channel delivery authority.
